name: Maisonneuve fracture
aliases: proximal fibular fracture with syndesmotic injury
high fibular fracture with mortise instability

reference.source: Rockwood and Green's Fractures in Adults
clinicalPearls: A proximal fibular fracture combined with disruption of the interosseous membrane and syndesmosis and a medial ankle injury (either a medial malleolus fracture or a deltoid ligament rupture)
An external-rotation force drives energy up the interosseous membrane, exiting proximally in the fibula
The proximal fibula must be palpated in every ankle injury; proximal tenderness or a medial injury with a widened mortise mandates imaging of the whole leg
The ankle mortise may be widened at the medial clear space despite an apparently isolated medial malleolar injury
Treatment focuses on restoring the mortise and stabilising the syndesmosis with a screw or suture-button construct; the proximal fibular fracture itself is usually not fixed
The injury is easily missed when the proximal fibula is neither examined nor imaged
Assess and document common peroneal nerve function at the fibular neck
reference.pathophysiology: A pronation-external rotation force at the ankle is transmitted proximally through the interosseous membrane. As the talus externally rotates, the syndesmosis and interosseous membrane tear and the energy exits as a fracture of the proximal fibula, while the medial restraint fails either as a deltoid ligament rupture or a medial malleolus fracture. The result is an unstable ankle mortise despite an intact distal fibula, and the key to a good outcome is anatomical reduction of the syndesmosis rather than the proximal fracture.
additionalDifferentials: Isolated ankle fracture (Weber A or B pattern)
Proximal fibular fracture from direct trauma
additionalInvestigations: Full-length tibia and fibula radiographs in addition to a dedicated ankle series
Ankle mortise view assessing the medial clear space for widening
Stress or weight-bearing views to demonstrate syndesmotic instability
CT to evaluate the adequacy of syndesmotic reduction
Examination and documentation of common peroneal nerve function
redFlags: Common peroneal nerve injury at the fibular neck
A widened mortise indicating an unstable ankle
reference.prognosis: With anatomical restoration of the mortise and adequate syndesmotic fixation the outcome is generally good; malreduction of the syndesmosis is the strongest predictor of pain and post-traumatic arthritis.
pitfalls: Failing to examine and image the proximal fibula in an ankle injury
Treating an apparently isolated medial malleolus fracture without recognising syndesmotic instability
Malreduction of the syndesmosis during fixation
Overlooking a common peroneal nerve injury
references: Rockwood and Green's Fractures in Adults
